title: Reassuring 'it's okay, you're not alone' consolation
description: This latent fires on short, formulaic reassurance phrases that normalize imperfection and failure, typically opening with 'Remember,' 'It's okay,' 'Nobody/No one is perfect,' or affirming 'That's okay!'/'We all do!' The activating text is direct, second- or first-person-plural comforting language explicitly telling the reader that mistakes, flaws, and struggles are normal and acceptable, often as a standalone sentence or closing line of advice. It does not activate on longer analytical or explanatory advice sentences that discuss a situation's nuance, give conditional judgments (e.g., 'It's possible that...', 'That being said...'), or provide practical instructions/tips without the core 'it's okay/you're not alone/nobody's perfect' consolation framing—even if those sentences are also supportive or empathetic in tone.
